Unchanged since R4; R4's 8/20 detection rate stands. What I added is the gap it leaves: this test excludes goroutines in ONE process. Ran the same shape across 6 separate processes (10 sections each, 3ms hold, IN/OUT interval log): 0 overlaps in 10 trials, while the unlink-on-release mutant produced 2-14 overlaps per trial (25 in 3). Cross-process exclusion therefore holds and the harness is discriminating. No multi-process exclusion test ships — a coverage limit, not a defect; not escalated.

Re-reported at the same standing, not escalated; byte-identical since R4. New ground: (a) .tp/locks creation failure — ENOTDIR (locks is a regular file) and EACCES (.tp at 0500) both return the wrapped 'create lock dir: %w', do NOT run fn and write nothing; tp add surfaces exit 1 JSON with a hint. (b) 6 processes x 10 sections: 0 interval overlaps in 10 trials vs 25 in 3 trials of an unlink-on-release mutant. (c) after SIGKILL/SIGTERM of a holder the next acquirer takes the lock in 3-5ms.

Unchanged since R4. Closed the orphaned-lock question R4 left open: while a subprocess holds the lock a second process times out at 1.04s with ran=false; after SIGKILL or SIGTERM of that holder the same lock file is reacquired in 3-5ms under the same name. The persisted zero-byte marker this file pins therefore creates no stale-lock deadlock — the lock lives on the fd, not on the file. Caveat: my first holder used select{}, which Go's deadlock detector killed.
